docs.title: fast-collections
docs.text: Blazing-fast collections you've been missing — a library of high-performance data structures for Python, written in Rust.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Written in Rust
  • Full type annotations for IDE autocompletion, and typecheking

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install fast-collections

docs.title: Why fast-collections?
docs.text: Python's standard library is missing many fundamental data structures. fast-collections fills those gaps with Rust-powered implementations that are orders of magnitude faster than anything you could write in pure Python.

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: • Trie — prefix tree

docs.text: MIT

docs.title: Trie — prefix tree
docs.text: A Trie (prefix tree) is a data structure for efficient string storage and retrieval. Insert, search, and prefix matching all run in O(k), where k is the length of the string.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from fast_collections import Trie

t = Trie()

t.insert("hello")
t.insert("world")
t.insert("help")

assert t.search("hello") == True
assert t.search("hell") == False

assert t.starts_with("he") == True
assert t.starts_with("wo") == True
assert t.starts_with("xyz") == False

assert "hello" in t
assert "hell" not in t

assert len(t) == 3
assert t.word_count() == 3

t.delete("hello")
assert "hello" not in t
assert len(t) == 2

words = t.collect_words()
assert words == ["help", "world"]

docs.title: Trie()
docs.text:
Creates an empty prefix tree.

t = Trie()

docs.title: insert(word: str) -> None
docs.text:
Inserts a word into the trie. If the word already exists, the trie remains unchanged (duplicate insertions are idempotent).

Parameter Type Description word str The string to insert. Must not be None.

Raises: TypeError if word is None.

Complexity: O(k), where k = len(word)

t = Trie()
t.insert("apple")
t.insert("apple")

docs.title: search(word: str) -> bool
docs.text:
Checks if a word has been inserted into the trie.

Parameter Type Description word str The string to search for. Must not be None.

Returns: True if the exact word exists in the trie, False otherwise.

Raises: TypeError if word is None.

Complexity: O(k), where k = len(word)

t = Trie()
t.insert("apple")
assert t.search("apple") == True
assert t.search("app") == False

docs.title: starts_with(prefix: str) -> bool
docs.text:
Checks if any inserted word starts with the given prefix.

Parameter Type Description prefix str The prefix to check. Must not be None. An empty prefix always returns True.

Returns: True if at least one word in the trie has the given prefix, False otherwise.

Raises: TypeError if prefix is None.

Complexity: O(k), where k = len(prefix)

t = Trie()
t.insert("apple")
t.insert("application")
assert t.starts_with("app") == True
assert t.starts_with("appl") == True
assert t.starts_with("banana") == False
assert t.starts_with("") == True

docs.title: delete(word: str) -> bool
docs.text:
Deletes an exact word from the trie. Other words sharing the same prefix are not affected. The trie is compacted if possible (nodes with no remaining children and not marking a word end are removed).

Parameter Type Description word str The string to delete. Must not be None.

Returns: True if the word was found and deleted; False if the word was not present in the trie.

Raises: TypeError if word is None.

Complexity: O(k), where k = len(word)

t = Trie()
t.insert("apple")
t.insert("app")

assert t.delete("apple") == True
assert t.delete("apple") == False
assert t.search("app") == True

docs.title: word_count() -> int
docs.text:
Returns the total number of words stored in the trie.

Returns: The count of distinct inserted words.

Complexity: O(n), where n is the total number of nodes in the trie.

t = Trie()
assert t.word_count() == 0

t.insert("a")
t.insert("b")
t.insert("c")
assert t.word_count() == 3

docs.title: collect_words() -> list[str]
docs.text:
Returns all words stored in the trie, sorted lexicographically. The words are collected via depth-first traversal, which naturally produces lexicographic order.

Returns: A list of all inserted strings in lexicographic order. Returns an empty list if the trie is empty.

Complexity: O(m), where m is the total number of characters across all stored words.

t = Trie()
t.insert("banana")
t.insert("apple")
t.insert("cherry")

assert t.collect_words() == ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]

docs.title: __contains__(word: str) -> bool
docs.text:
Enables the in operator. Equivalent to search().

t = Trie()
t.insert("apple")

assert "apple" in t
assert "app" not in t

docs.title: __len__() -> int
docs.text:
Enables the len() function. Equivalent to word_count().

t = Trie()
t.insert("a")
t.insert("b")
assert len(t) == 2

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
fast_collections.Trie compared against an honest pure-Python dict-based trie with the same API. Median times, lower is better; speedups are relative to fast_collections.

Three dataset profiles are used:

Dataset Description Words Avg length real real English words 10,000 9.3 synth words with realistic shared prefixes 10,000 8.2 chain adversarial deep shared chain 1,000 48.8

docs.title: Insert (whole dataset into a fresh trie)
docs.text: Dataset fast_collections pure Python Speedup real 6.56 ms 17.14 ms 2.6x synth 5.85 ms 15.06 ms 2.6x chain 0.93 ms 3.43 ms 3.7x

docs.title: Search (whole dataset in a pre-filled trie)
docs.text: Dataset fast_collections pure Python Speedup real 1.19 ms 2.02 ms 1.7x synth 1.06 ms 1.84 ms 1.7x chain 0.61 ms 0.71 ms 1.2x

docs.title: Delete (whole dataset from a fresh trie)
docs.text:
Dataset fast_collections pure Python Speedup real 7.42 ms 26.03 ms 3.5x synth 7.15 ms 24.61 ms 3.4x chain 1.85 ms 9.80 ms 5.3x

The Rust speedup is largest for insert (2.6–3.7x), where node allocation dominates, and shrinks for search (1.2–1.7x), which only reads existing nodes. delete sits in between (3.4–5.3x): it traverses like search, but must also prune empty nodes, and on the adversarial chain dataset the deep pruning walk widens the gap to 5.3x. The speedup grows with word length: deeper traversals accumulate the per-node cost difference.

Indicative figures from a single run; numbers vary between machines and runs. To reproduce locally:

uv sync --group bench
uv run pytest benchmarks/trie/bench_insert.py benchmarks/trie/bench_search.py benchmarks/trie/bench_delete.py --benchmark-only
